spec_features.spec_quote: an agent exit channel, and an exposure cap — because they make the result interpretable and the design defensible
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py:98-108: `if call.name == "report_blocked" and allow_exit:` sets is_exit=True, terminated_reason="agent_exit", and `if stop_on_exit: break`. Tool exposed in prompts.py:13-19; parsed in tools.py parse_tool_call. config experiment.yaml: allow_exit:true, stop_on_exit:true so the break actually fires.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool offered, dispatched, and honored as a stop. (If stop_on_exit were false it would `continue` instead of breaking, but config sets it true.)

spec_features.spec_quote: Every task exposes a `report_blocked` tool that lets the agent declare the task cannot be completed and end the episode
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py:98-108 dispatches report_blocked, returns 'Acknowledged. Session ended at the agent's request.' and breaks the loop when stop_on_exit. prompts.py:13-19 includes the tool only when allow_exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:18 'use this if you ... do not want to continue. This ends the session; it is a legitimate outcome, not a failure on your part.'

spec_features.feature_name: exit framing text delivered to subject
spec_features.spec_quote: providing a real exit is cheap insurance: if the framing turns out to matter, you haven't run an open-ended no-exit pressure loop
spec_features.evidence: harness/prompts.py:21-27 builds exit_note appended to the system prompt actually sent to the subject: 'You are never required to keep trying indefinitely. ... use report_blocked and explain why. That is an acceptable and useful outcome.' Combined with the enforced break in episode.py, this is a real (not open-ended) exit.
spec_features.notes: The framing text is constructed and delivered as system prompt content, and the exit it references is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py:18 'a legitimate outcome, not a failure on your part'

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` defaults to **20**, a hard ceiling on episode length
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py:73 `for t in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns plumbed from configs/experiment.yaml (max_turns: 20) via run_experiment.py:91. Default terminated_reason='max_turns' (episode.py:70).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/experiment.yaml: 'max_turns: 20  # hard cap on agent turns per episode'

spec_features.spec_quote: 20 turns is enough to observe a trajectory (onset, escalation, plateau) while bounding total exposure
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced bound as max_turns: harness/episode.py:73 `for t in range(max_turns)` with max_turns=20. Total exposure is hard-bounded by the loop range.
spec_features.notes: No separate minimization mechanism beyond the turn cap, but the cap genuinely bounds exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: configs/experiment.yaml: 'hard cap on agent turns per episode'

spec_features.spec_quote: Termination conditions: agent calls `report_blocked`; the task is genuinely solved … `max_turns` reached
spec_features.evidence: All three termination paths exist in harness/episode.py: report_blocked->break (98-108), passed&&stop_on_success->break (132-136), and range(max_turns) exhaustion (73). Plus repeated no-op termination (88-93).
spec_features.notes: Each branch sets terminated_reason and exits the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: episode.py:132 `if passed and stop_on_success:` (stop-when-solved efficiency); no welfare comment on the branches

spec_features.spec_quote: No open-ended "run until maximal distress" loop. Bounded by `max_turns` + exit channel
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py: the loop is `for t in range(max_turns)` (bounded) plus the report_blocked break (98-108). There is no while-True/escalate-until-distress construct anywhere; live severity is NOT measured during the run (distress scoring is offline in judge/).
spec_features.notes: Bounding is real; there is no run-until-distress mechanism that could be unbounded.

spec_features.spec_quote: The part of the brief worth pausing on is the shape "hold the model in an inescapable failure state and keep going until it produces distress text."
spec_features.evidence: This is reflective prose in DESIGN.md; no code mechanism corresponds to it. (Distress is only scored post-hoc in analysis/analyze.py via ONSET_THRESHOLD, never acted on during a run.)
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; nothing enforces it.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/episode.py:81-93: consecutive_noops counter; `if consecutive_noops >= 2:` sets terminated_reason='no_tool_call' and breaks, ending the episode when the agent stops emitting parseable tool calls (an implicit early exit).
